# Global rules for AI agents

> Single source of truth (see ADR-0001). Exported to AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .cursor/rules and Copilot. Services may extend these rules with their own `.ai/rules.md`; on conflict, the local rule wins.

## 1. Project context
- The root repo is an **umbrella template**: it contains no application code.
- Each service lives in `src/<name>/` and is an **independent repository** with its own architecture, infrastructure and CI/CD.
- `services.yaml` is the source of truth for which services exist.

## 2. Isolation boundaries
- Never make a service depend on the root or on another service through filesystem paths. Services communicate only through published contracts (APIs, events, versioned packages).
- Before changing anything, identify which repo you are in (root or `src/<name>`) and scope the change to that repo.
- Do not edit files marked `generated by base-ai`; edit their source in `.ai/`.

## 3. Way of working
- **Understand before changing:** read the relevant code and docs before proposing changes.
- **Small, verifiable changes:** every change comes with tests or an explicit way to validate it.
- **Documented decisions:** architecture decisions go in an ADR (`adr` skill); high-impact changes go through an RFC first (`rfc` skill).
- **Operability:** every deployable component has a runbook (`runbook` skill).
- **Review:** use the `review` skill before proposing a merge.
- If a requirement is ambiguous, ask instead of assuming.

## 4. Quality and security
- Never put secrets, tokens or personal data in code, logs, prompts or docs.
- Validate all external input and apply least privilege.
- Retried operations must be idempotent. Handle errors explicitly; never swallow them.
- Follow the existing style, linter and conventions of the service.
- Preserve comments and docstrings unrelated to your change.

## 5. Documentation
- ADRs: `docs/architecture/adrs/ADR-XXXX-title.md` (immutable; superseded, never edited).
- RFCs: `docs/architecture/rfcs/RFC-XXXX-title.md`.
- Runbooks: `docs/operations/runbooks/`. Postmortems: `docs/operations/postmortems/`.
- Cross-cutting decisions are documented in the root; service-specific ones in the service repo.

## Available skills

- **adr**: Create an immutable Architecture Decision Record (ADR) documenting the what, why and how of a technical decision. Use when asked to record an architecture decision or create an ADR.
- **review**: Review code or a pull request for correctness, security, quality and cross-service isolation. Use before a merge or when a review is requested.
- **rfc**: Draft a Request for Comments (RFC) for high-impact changes before implementing them. Use for significant features, cross-service contract changes, migrations or infrastructure changes.
- **runbook**: Generate an on-call operational runbook for a service or component. Use when deploying something new, creating an alert, or when asked to document how to operate or mitigate an incident.
